correctness.rationale: The transition encoding follows from binary Thue-Morse. For n=2^j, the three n-blocks have N1 counts A0=A2 odd and A1 2 mod 4. M1 modulo n separates within outside groups, and within middle groups up to half-turn. The outside groups are exchanged by 0/2 with odd zero-minus-two imbalance; the middle half-turn changes M0 because its zero count is odd. Four moments follow from scattered length-2 binomial coefficients. Thus the first 3n windows have distinct 2-binomial signatures; published exact p_x(n)=3n finishes. The proof establishes all j>=2. Executable verification independently checks all claims for j=2..10; finite tests alone were not used as proof.

value.rationale: This establishes a natural infinite subsequence-complexity invariant at all dyadic lengths of the canonical squarefree ternary Thue word. It shows that order-two scattered-subsequence multiplicities exactly distinguish all 3n contiguous factors, sharply contrasting with bounded binomial complexity for binary Thue-Morse and the different all-length rigidity of Tribonacci. The proof gives a simple four-integer distinguishing fingerprint from letter counts and positional moments rather than just a finite table. Other lengths remain open.
